label: Foundation: Conditioning & Strength Base
summary: Build a durable full-body strength and conditioning base that fits a busy, unpredictable week and protects your joints for the long run.
outcomes: A full-body strength base that survives a missed or reshuffled day
Real conditioning capacity from two dedicated cardio-quality sessions
Joint-friendly training that counters a desk-bound routine
Simple, repeatable technique before intensity ever gets added
description:
This first phase builds the foundation everything else depends on: a full-body strength base, real conditioning capacity, and joint-friendly movement patterns that hold up against a busy, unpredictable week - without chasing muscle size or heavy numbers yet.

Three full-body strength sessions anchor the week, with two lower-fatigue conditioning days and your existing sport/class session filling out the rest. Loads start conservatively around RPE 6 - add the smallest practical load only once every rep looks clean.

Move on once all five weekly sessions are completed consistently, technique feels repeatable across the main lifts, and RPE 6-7 loads keep progressing symptom-free for two straight weeks - that's the signal for a general strength-and-conditioning build next.

days.label: Session 1
days.focus: Full-Body Anchor A - Squat & Vertical Patterns

items.name: Easy Bike or Row Spin-Up
items.cue: Raise core temperature and get the joints moving before loading anything.

items.name: Hip & Ankle Mobility Flow
items.dose: 2 rounds: 5 each side, hip openers + ankle rocks
items.cue: Open the hips and ankles this session's squat pattern needs.

items.name: Glute & Core Activation
items.cue: Wake up the muscles doing the real work today before the load does.

items.name: Goblet Squat
items.cue: Sit down between your hips, chest tall - this is your main squat pattern for the week.

items.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
items.cue: Press straight overhead without arching the lower back - control beats load here.

items.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
items.cue: Pull with the elbow, not the hand - this is the pulling work a desk day never gives you.

items.name: Cable Pallof Press
items.cue: Resist the cable pulling you sideways - think stiff, not strong.

items.name: Kettlebell Swing (Quality Reps)
items.cue: Snap the hips, not the arms. Stop the set the moment reps look effortful instead of explosive.

items.name: Lat & Chest Doorway Stretch
items.cue: Undo the day's forward-rounded posture before you leave the gym.

items.name: Thoracic Extension & Rotation
items.cue: This is the mobility a desk job takes away - reclaim it before it gets stiff.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
items.cue: Long sitting shortens this muscle - give it real time under tension, not a quick pull.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cue: Build hip rotation a chair never asks of you.

items.name: Steady Aerobic - Treadmill, Rower or Bike (your choice)
perRound: Hold a conversational pace throughout - this builds recovery capacity, it isn't a hard effort.
items.cue: You should be able to hold a conversation the entire way through.

items.name: Dead Bug
items.cue: Keep the low back flat on the floor - this is control, not a rep count to rush.

items.name: Full-Body Static Stretch Flow
items.cue: Slow everything down before you leave.

days.label: Session 3
days.focus: Full-Body Anchor B - Hinge & Horizontal Push

items.name: Easy Bike or Row Spin-Up
items.cue: Same purpose as every session - raise temperature before loading the hips.

items.name: Glute Bridge + Cat-Cow Flow
items.cue: Prime the hinge pattern and free up the spine before the trap bar.

items.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
items.cue: Push the floor away with your legs, chest tall - the safest way into real hinge loading.

items.name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
items.cue: Lower under control - the eccentric is where beginners build the most durable strength.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Rear Foot Elevated)
items.cue: Most of your weekly training is bilateral - this is where single-leg stability gets built.

items.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Carry
items.cue: Walk tall and resist leaning - the core is working to keep you upright, not to move anything.

items.name: Broad Jump (Stick the Landing)
items.cue: Jump for distance, land soft and still. Stop the set once the landings stop being crisp.

items.name: Hip Flexor & Hamstring Stretch
items.cue: The hinge pattern loads the hamstrings hard - give them a proper stretch on the way out.

days.label: Session 4
days.focus: Existing sport / class session (external - not authored here)

items.name: Easy Bike or Row Spin-Up
items.cue: Consistent warm-up every anchor day - raise temperature before pulling load.

items.name: Shoulder Circles + Scap Push-Ups
items.cue: Prep the shoulder blades for pulling work - exactly what a desk-rounded posture needs.

items.name: Pull-Up (or Feet-Elevated Inverted Row Under the Rack Bar)
items.reps: As many clean reps as possible, or 8-10 on the row regression

prescription.note: Stop 1-2 reps before failure. The regression is not a lesser exercise - it is the right choice at this stage.

items.cue: Pick whichever version lets you finish every rep with full range and no straining.

items.name: Functional Trainer Chest Press
items.cue: The cable path is more joint-friendly than a fixed bar - let the machine guide the groove.

items.name: Leg Press
items.cue: A supported way to add real leg volume without extra spinal loading on top of the squat day.

items.name: Hanging Knee Raise
items.cue: Lift with the lower abs, not momentum - a slow rep beats a swinging one.

items.name: Box Jump (Step Down, Not Down-Jump)
items.cue: Jump up with intent, then step back down - the landing is where beginners get hurt, not the jump.

items.name: Lat, Chest & Hip Flexor Stretch Flow
items.cue: Close out the week's third anchor session the same way you started it - unwind what you just loaded.

items.name: Dynamic Full-Body Warm-Up
items.dose: 5 min: light cardio + leg swings + arm circles
items.cue: Short and purposeful - the real work today is the intervals.

items.name: Controlled Intervals - Bike, Rower or SkiErg (your choice)
perRound: R1-2: Build into a strong, controlled pace
R3-4: Hold the pace, breathing hard but controlled
R5-6: Same pace - resist the urge to empty the tank
items.cue: Controlled means hard but repeatable - if round 6 looks nothing like round 1, the pace was too aggressive.

items.name: Plank
items.cue: A quiet plank beats a shaking one - stop the set when form breaks, not when the clock says so.

items.name: Easy Walk + Full-Body Stretch
items.cue: Bring the heart rate down gradually before you stop moving.
